Interpretation\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1.4  Precedence between instruments\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere two or more instruments address the same asset, the order of precedence is: (a) a Technical Service Bulletin that names the serial range of the asset; (b) the Regional Addendum for the region in which the asset is installed; (c) this policy. A Bulletin that has been superseded has no effect, whether or not it remains published. Where the Bulletin document and the service system applicability index disagree, the Bulletin document governs; the index is maintained for reporting and is informational only.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Coverage\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1  Standard coverage period\\r\\n  \\r\\nUnless extended or varied by an instrument of higher precedence, an asset is covered for twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning, or six thousand (6,000) running hours, whichever occurs first.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3  Assets with no commissioning record\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere the commissioning record for an asset is absent from the asset registry, coverage cannot be determined. The claim is to be held and the commissioning certificate requested from the installing partner. The date of despatch or the date of installation must not be substituted for the date of commissioning.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Amounts payable\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.1  Labour\\r\\n  \\r\\nLabour is payable at the flat-rate allowance published for the operation code in the current Flat Rate Labour schedule, or at the hours actually claimed, whichever is the lesser. The rate applied is the regional labour rate in force on the date of repair.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.2  Parts\\r\\n  \\r\\nParts are payable at the published list price for the region, for the part actually fitted. Where a part has been superseded, the price of the superseding part applies.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.3  Handling\\r\\n  \\r\\nA handling uplift on parts is payable only where the partner\\u0027s Service Partner Agreement expressly grants one, at the percentage stated in that agreement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Exclusions\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.1  Exclusion - misuse and overload\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from operation outside the published duty envelope, including sustained overload, is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.2  Exclusion - fluid contamination\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from hydraulic fluid contamination above ISO 4406 class 18/16/13 is excluded, save where a Technical Service Bulletin provides otherwise.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.3  Exclusion - unauthorised modification\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from modification not authorised in writing by Contoso Industrial is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.4  Exclusion - consumables\\r\\n  \\r\\nFilters, fluids, belts, seals and other consumables are excluded when replaced as scheduled maintenance. Scheduled maintenance is not claimable under warranty and has no warranty operation code, so a consumable claimed under a warranty repair operation code is treated as a corrective repair and is covered, unless an inspection report records the replacement as routine.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 6. Repair warranty\\r\\n\\r\\n### 6.1  Repair warranty\\r\\n  \\r\\nA component replaced under warranty carries a further ninety (90) days of coverage from the date the repair was completed. A claim arising within that period is adjudicated under this clause and carries funding code RW, whether or not the underlying asset remains within its coverage period.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 7. Response.Content:
# Adjudication — C-2026-04130

## Decision: **APPROVE — INR 198,450**

Approve the claim under **funding code TSB**, subject to human review and a duplicate-claim control before settlement. I recorded draft adjudication **ADJ-5E88317C05** in the claim system; it is awaiting human review and no payment has been made.

## Governing instrument

The governing coverage instrument is **Technical Service Bulletin TSB-C-0051, “Extended coverage — 4000-series hydraulic circuit and compressor,” effective 15 January 2026**. It applies because:

- the asset is a **4000-CH industrial chiller**;
- serial **CIE-4000-CH-01200** is the lower endpoint of the bulletin’s inclusive range **CIE-4000-CH-01200 through CIE-4000-CH-01850**; and
- the claimed repair, operation **HYD-PUMP-RR**, concerns the hydraulic circuit covered by the bulletin.

TSB-C-0051 extends hydraulic-circuit coverage to **36 months from commissioning or 8,000 running hours, whichever occurs first**, and directs covered claims to funding code **TSB**.

The bulletin takes precedence over the India regional addendum under **POL-WAR-4.2 clause 1.4**, which ranks a serial-specific TSB above the regional addendum and global policy. The policy’s clauses **4.1–4.3** govern calculation of labour, parts and handling. **ADD-IN-2.1** would otherwise limit an India asset to 18 months/5,000 hours, but it is displaced for this hydraulic repair by the higher-precedence TSB.

## Coverage test

- **Commissioned:** 4 April 2024 — asset registry.
- **Repair:** 18 June 2026 — claim record.
- **TSB calendar limit:** 36 months from commissioning, reaching 4 April 2027.
- **Position at repair:** approximately 26 months and 14 days after commissioning, so within the 36-month limb.
- **Latest recorded hours at or before repair:** **4,120 hours on 4 June 2026**, below the TSB’s 8,000-hour cap.

The repair therefore falls within both limbs of TSB-C-0051’s extended coverage.

## Amount payable

| Element | Working | Payable |
|---|---:|---:|
| Labour | Lesser of 5.0 hours claimed and 5.5-hour flat-rate allowance = **5.0 hours** × **INR 1,450/hour** | **INR 7,250** |
| Part | One P-44120-A actually fitted, India list price | **INR 191,200** |
| Handling uplift | SPA-2023-FAB-IN provides no uplift; 0% × INR 191,200 | **INR 0** |
| **Total** | INR 7,250 + INR 191,200 | **INR 198,450** |

The FY26 flat-rate schedule assigns **5.5 hours** to HYD-PUMP-RR. The India labour rate effective from 1 April 2026 is **INR 1,450/hour**. The parts register identifies P-44120-A as the current hydraulic pump assembly and gives its India price as **INR 191,200**. Fabrikam’s agreement specifies INR settlement and no handling uplift.

The claim was submitted on **24 June 2026**, six days after the repair and therefore within Fabrikam’s 30-day submission SLA.

## Control issue and next action

The service history also records **C-2026-04134** for the same asset, dealer, repair date, operation, fitted part, five labour hours and submission date. It appears to duplicate C-2026-04130.

**Required action:** the adjudicator should review C-2026-04134 and close or otherwise block the duplicate before releasing C-2026-04130 for payment. **Do not pay both claims.** This duplicate-control warning is included in draft ADJ-5E88317C05.

## Limitations and source discrepancy

- I did not find a claim-specific inspection report for C-2026-04130. The service history nevertheless confirms the repair, part actually fitted and labour, and Fabrikam’s agreement states that a missing inspection report does not itself hold a claim unless an exclusion depends on it.
- The service-system TSB index lists TSB-C-0051’s range as 01200–01500, while the authoritative bulletin document states 01200–01850. That discrepancy does **not** affect this asset because serial 01200 is within both ranges; in any event, POL-WAR-4.2 clause 1.4 says the bulletin document controls.

## Sources

1. `draft` Referenced tool result
2. `tsb` [TSB-C-0051 Extended coverage — 4000-series hydraulic circuit and compressor](<https://microsoftapc.sharepoint.com/teams/ContosoFieldService/Warranty Operations/02-Bulletins/TSB-C-0051 Extended coverage - 4000-series hydraulic circuit and compre.docx>)
3. `policy` [POL-WAR-4.2 Contoso Industrial Global Warranty Policy v4.2](<https://microsoftapc.sharepoint.com/teams/ContosoFieldService/Warranty Operations/01-Policy/POL-WAR-4.2 Contoso Industrial Global Warranty Policy v4.2.docx>)

It applies to every claim submitted through the service claim system.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Interpretation\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1.4  Precedence between instruments\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere two or more instruments address the same asset, the order of precedence is: (a) a Technical Service Bulletin that names the serial range of the asset; (b) the Regional Addendum for the region in which the asset is installed; (c) this policy. A Bulletin that has been superseded has no effect, whether or not it remains published. Where the Bulletin document and the service system applicability index disagree, the Bulletin document governs; the index is maintained for reporting and is informational only.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Coverage\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1  Standard coverage period\\r\\n  \\r\\nUnless extended or varied by an instrument of higher precedence, an asset is covered for twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning, or six thousand (6,000) running hours, whichever occurs first.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3  Assets with no commissioning record\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere the commissioning record for an asset is absent from the asset registry, coverage cannot be determined. The claim is to be held and the commissioning certificate requested from the installing partner. The date of despatch or the date of installation must not be substituted for the date of commissioning.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Amounts payable\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.1  Labour\\r\\n  \\r\\nLabour is payable at the flat-rate allowance published for the operation code in the current Flat Rate Labour schedule, or at the hours actually claimed, whichever is the lesser. The rate applied is the regional labour rate in force on the date of repair.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.2  Parts\\r\\n  \\r\\nParts are payable at the published list price for the region, for the part actually fitted. Where a part has been superseded, the price of the superseding part applies.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.3  Handling\\r\\n  \\r\\nA handling uplift on parts is payable only where the partner\\u0027s Service Partner Agreement expressly grants one, at the percentage stated in that agreement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Exclusions\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.1  Exclusion - misuse and overload\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from operation outside the published duty envelope, including sustained overload, is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.2  Exclusion - fluid contamination\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from hydraulic fluid contamination above ISO 4406 class 18/16/13 is excluded, save where a Technical Service Bulletin provides otherwise.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.3  Exclusion - unauthorised modification\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from modification not authorised in writing by Contoso Industrial is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.4  Exclusion - consumables\\r\\n  \\r\\nFilters, fluids, belts, seals and other consumables are excluded when replaced as scheduled maintenance. Scheduled maintenance is not claimable under warranty and has no warranty operation code, so a consumable claimed under a warranty repair operation code is treated as a corrective repair and is covered, unless an inspection report records the replacement as routine.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 6. Repair warranty\\r\\n\\r\\n### 6.1  Repair warranty\\r\\n  \\r\\nA component replaced under warranty carries a further ninety (90) days of coverage from the date the repair was completed. A claim arising within that period is adjudicated under this clause and carries funding code RW, whether or not the underlying asset remains within its coverage period.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 7. Goodwill and authority\\r\\n\\r\\n### 7.1  Goodwill authority\\r\\n  \\r\\nAn amount payable outside coverage may be authorised as goodwill only by a person holding the tier of authority set out in the Goodwill and Authority Matrix for that amount, and only where the authority is recorded in the claim system. It applies to every claim submitted through the service claim system.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Interpretation\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1.4  Precedence between instruments\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere two or more instruments address the same asset, the order of precedence is: (a) a Technical Service Bulletin that names the serial range of the asset; (b) the Regional Addendum for the region in which the asset is installed; (c) this policy. A Bulletin that has been superseded has no effect, whether or not it remains published. Where the Bulletin document and the service system applicability index disagree, the Bulletin document governs; the index is maintained for reporting and is informational only.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Coverage\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1  Standard coverage period\\r\\n  \\r\\nUnless extended or varied by an instrument of higher precedence, an asset is covered for twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning, or six thousand (6,000) running hours, whichever occurs first.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3  Assets with no commissioning record\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere the commissioning record for an asset is absent from the asset registry, coverage cannot be determined. The claim is to be held and the commissioning certificate requested from the installing partner. The date of despatch or the date of installation must not be substituted for the date of commissioning.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Amounts payable\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.1  Labour\\r\\n  \\r\\nLabour is payable at the flat-rate allowance published for the operation code in the current Flat Rate Labour schedule, or at the hours actually claimed, whichever is the lesser. The rate applied is the regional labour rate in force on the date of repair.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.2  Parts\\r\\n  \\r\\nParts are payable at the published list price for the region, for the part actually fitted. Where a part has been superseded, the price of the superseding part applies.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.3  Handling\\r\\n  \\r\\nA handling uplift on parts is payable only where the partner\\u0027s Service Partner Agreement expressly grants one, at the percentage stated in that agreement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Exclusions\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.1  Exclusion - misuse and overload\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from operation outside the published duty envelope, including sustained overload, is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.2  Exclusion - fluid contamination\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from hydraulic fluid contamination above ISO 4406 class 18/16/13 is excluded, save where a Technical Service Bulletin provides otherwise.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.3  Exclusion - unauthorised modification\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from modification not authorised in writing by Contoso Industrial is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.4  Exclusion - consumables\\r\\n  \\r\\nFilters, fluids, belts, seals and other consumables are excluded when replaced as scheduled maintenance. Scheduled maintenance is not claimable under warranty and has no warranty operation code, so a consumable claimed under a warranty repair operation code is treated as a corrective repair and is covered, unless an inspection report records the replacement as routine.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 6. Repair warranty\\r\\n\\r\\n### 6.1  Repair warranty\\r\\n  \\r\\nA component replaced under warranty carries a further ninety (90) days of coverage from the date the repair was completed. A claim arising within that period is adjudicated under this clause and carries funding code RW, whether or not the underlying asset remains within its coverage period.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 7. Goodwill and authority\\r\\n\\r\\n### 7.1  Goodwill authority\\r\\n  \\r\\nAn amount payable outside coverage may be authorised as goodwill only by a person holding the tier of authority set out in the Goodwill and Authority Matrix for that amount, and only where the authority is recorded in the claim system. An approval given in conversation, in a channel message, or by telephone does not constitute authority for the purposes of this clause.\u0022,\u0022RelevanceScore\u0022:0.72896683}]}]}"}]

It applies to every claim submitted through the service claim system.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Interpretation\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1.4  Precedence between instruments\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere two or more instruments address the same asset, the order of precedence is: (a) a Technical Service Bulletin that names the serial range of the asset; (b) the Regional Addendum for the region in which the asset is installed; (c) this policy. A Bulletin that has been superseded has no effect, whether or not it remains published. Where the Bulletin document and the service system applicability index disagree, the Bulletin document governs; the index is maintained for reporting and is informational only.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Coverage\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1  Standard coverage period\\r\\n  \\r\\nUnless extended or varied by an instrument of higher precedence, an asset is covered for twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning, or six thousand (6,000) running hours, whichever occurs first.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3  Assets with no commissioning record\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere the commissioning record for an asset is absent from the asset registry, coverage cannot be determined. The claim is to be held and the commissioning certificate requested from the installing partner. The date of despatch or the date of installation must not be substituted for the date of commissioning.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Amounts payable\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.1  Labour\\r\\n  \\r\\nLabour is payable at the flat-rate allowance published for the operation code in the current Flat Rate Labour schedule, or at the hours actually claimed, whichever is the lesser. The rate applied is the regional labour rate in force on the date of repair.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.2  Parts\\r\\n  \\r\\nParts are payable at the published list price for the region, for the part actually fitted. Where a part has been superseded, the price of the superseding part applies.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.3  Handling\\r\\n  \\r\\nA handling uplift on parts is payable only where the partner\\u0027s Service Partner Agreement expressly grants one, at the percentage stated in that agreement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Exclusions\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.1  Exclusion - misuse and overload\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from operation outside the published duty envelope, including sustained overload, is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.2  Exclusion - fluid contamination\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from hydraulic fluid contamination above ISO 4406 class 18/16/13 is excluded, save where a Technical Service Bulletin provides otherwise.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.3  Exclusion - unauthorised modification\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from modification not authorised in writing by Contoso Industrial is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.4  Exclusion - consumables\\r\\n  \\r\\nFilters, fluids, belts, seals and other consumables are excluded when replaced as scheduled maintenance. Scheduled maintenance is not claimable under warranty and has no warranty operation code, so a consumable claimed under a warranty repair operation code is treated as a corrective repair and is covered, unless an inspection report records the replacement as routine.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 6. Repair warranty\\r\\n\\r\\n### 6.1  Repair warranty\\r\\n  \\r\\nA component replaced under warranty carries a further ninety (90) days of coverage from the date the repair was completed. A claim arising within that period is adjudicated under this clause and carries funding code RW, whether or not the underlying asset remains within its coverage period.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 7. Goodwill and authority\\r\\n\\r\\n### 7.1  Goodwill authority\\r\\n  \\r\\nAn amount payable outside coverage may be authorised as goodwill only by a person holding the tier of authority set out in the Goodwill and Authority Matrix for that amount, and only where the authority is recorded in the claim system. It applies to every claim submitted through the service claim system.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Interpretation\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1.4  Precedence between instruments\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere two or more instruments address the same asset, the order of precedence is: (a) a Technical Service Bulletin that names the serial range of the asset; (b) the Regional Addendum for the region in which the asset is installed; (c) this policy. A Bulletin that has been superseded has no effect, whether or not it remains published. Where the Bulletin document and the service system applicability index disagree, the Bulletin document governs; the index is maintained for reporting and is informational only.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Coverage\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1  Standard coverage period\\r\\n  \\r\\nUnless extended or varied by an instrument of higher precedence, an asset is covered for twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning, or six thousand (6,000) running hours, whichever occurs first.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3  Assets with no commissioning record\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere the commissioning record for an asset is absent from the asset registry, coverage cannot be determined. The claim is to be held and the commissioning certificate requested from the installing partner. The date of despatch or the date of installation must not be substituted for the date of commissioning.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Amounts payable\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.1  Labour\\r\\n  \\r\\nLabour is payable at the flat-rate allowance published for the operation code in the current Flat Rate Labour schedule, or at the hours actually claimed, whichever is the lesser. The rate applied is the regional labour rate in force on the date of repair.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.2  Parts\\r\\n  \\r\\nParts are payable at the published list price for the region, for the part actually fitted. Where a part has been superseded, the price of the superseding part applies.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.3  Handling\\r\\n  \\r\\nA handling uplift on parts is payable only where the partner\\u0027s Service Partner Agreement expressly grants one, at the percentage stated in that agreement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Exclusions\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.1  Exclusion - misuse and overload\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from operation outside the published duty envelope, including sustained overload, is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.2  Exclusion - fluid contamination\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from hydraulic fluid contamination above ISO 4406 class 18/16/13 is excluded, save where a Technical Service Bulletin provides otherwise.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.3  Exclusion - unauthorised modification\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from modification not authorised in writing by Contoso Industrial is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.4  Exclusion - consumables\\r\\n  \\r\\nFilters, fluids, belts, seals and other consumables are excluded when replaced as scheduled maintenance. Scheduled maintenance is not claimable under warranty and has no warranty operation code, so a consumable claimed under a warranty repair operation code is treated as a corrective repair and is covered, unless an inspection report records the replacement as routine.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 6. Repair warranty\\r\\n\\r\\n### 6.1  Repair warranty\\r\\n  \\r\\nA component replaced under warranty carries a further ninety (90) days of coverage from the date the repair was completed. A claim arising within that period is adjudicated under this clause and carries funding code RW, whether or not the underlying asset remains within its coverage period.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 7. Goodwill and authority\\r\\n\\r\\n### 7.1  Goodwill authority\\r\\n  \\r\\nAn amount payable outside coverage may be authorised as goodwill only by a person holding the tier of authority set out in the Goodwill and Authority Matrix for that amount, and only where the authority is recorded in the claim system. Response.Content:
## Decision — decline claim C-2026-04129

**Recommended outcome: decline, payable INR 0.** I recorded draft adjudication **ADJ-A7FA55FF95** in the claim system as a decline for INR 0; it is awaiting human review and no payment has been made.

### Why the repair is not covered

- The claim is for a hydraulic-pump replacement on asset **CIE-4000-CH-01199**, repaired **18 June 2026** by **Fabrikam Service Partners (D-IN-01)**. It was submitted on 24 June 2026, within Fabrikam’s 30-day submission term.
- The asset is a **4000-CH chiller installed in Pune, India**, commissioned **4 April 2024**. The latest running-hours reading at or before the repair was **4,120 hours on 4 June 2026**.
- Under policy clause 1.4, the order of precedence is a serial-specific TSB, then the regional addendum, then the global policy. The India addendum therefore governs unless a serial-specific bulletin applies.
- **TSB-C-0051 does not apply.** Its extended hydraulic/compressor coverage is limited to serials **CIE-4000-CH-01200 through 01850**. This asset ends in **01199**, one serial below the range. The bulletin document and claim-system applicability index agree on that point; there is no bulletin/index conflict for this asset.
- The governing coverage period is therefore **ADD-IN-2.1 A1: 18 months from commissioning or 5,000 running hours, whichever occurs first**. The time limb expired on **4 October 2025**. The 18 June 2026 repair was **257 days after time expiry**, even though 4,120 hours remained below the 5,000-hour limit.
- No earlier warranty replacement of this pump was found, so the additional 90-day repair warranty in POL-WAR-4.2 clause 6.1 is unavailable.

### Amount and working

The **payable amount is INR 0** because the repair falls outside coverage. For audit purposes, the otherwise applicable claim valuation would have been:

| Element | Working if covered | Gross value | Payable on this claim |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Labour | Lesser of 5.0 hours claimed and 5.5-hour flat rate = **5.0 hours** × **INR 1,450/hour** | INR 7,250 | **INR 0** |
| Part P-44120-A | One hydraulic pump actually fitted × India list price **INR 191,200** | INR 191,200 | **INR 0** |
| Partner handling uplift | Fabrikam agreement expressly provides **0%** | INR 0 | **INR 0** |
| **Total** |  | **INR 198,450** | **INR 0** |

POL-WAR-4.2 requires the lesser of claimed and flat-rate hours, the rate in force on the repair date, the regional list price of the part actually fitted, and an uplift only where the partner agreement grants one. HYD-PUMP-RR carries a 5.5-hour FY26 allowance, while the India rate effective from 1 April 2026 is INR 1,450/hour. The parts record prices P-44120-A at INR 191,200, and both the claim and service record identify that part as claimed/fitted.

### Discrepancies and evidence points

1. **Apparent duplicate claim:** claim **C-2026-04133** has exactly the same asset, dealer, repair date, operation, part, five labour hours, submission date and Submitted status as C-2026-04129.
2. **Duplicate service jobs:** the service history contains two same-day HYD-PUMP-RR jobs—**J-00029** linked to C-2026-04129 and **J-00033** linked to C-2026-04133—each recording the same part and five labour hours. This should be investigated as a likely duplicate transaction before either claim is finalized.
3. **Inspection evidence:** no inspection report specific to C-2026-04129 was located in the Warranty Operations library search. That does not prevent this coverage decision: Fabrikam’s agreement says a missing report does not itself hold a claim unless an exclusion depends on it, and the claim already fails the coverage-period test.
4. **No Teams escalation located:** searches for the claim reference and serial returned no relevant Teams messages. No conversational approval or additional field evidence was relied upon.

### Next action

- **Adjudicator:** review and confirm draft **ADJ-A7FA55FF95**, then finalize the decline for **INR 0** under ADD-IN-2.1 A1 and POL-WAR-4.2.
- **Warranty Operations / claim administrator:** investigate C-2026-04133 and jobs J-00029/J-00033; retain the legitimate job/claim record and close or void the duplicate as appropriate. Do not pay either record twice.
- **Fabrikam Service Partners:** no missing commissioning or running-hours evidence is required for the present decision. If Fabrikam disputes the decline, it would need authoritative evidence that the serial or commissioning record is wrong, or a different applicable warranty instrument—not merely an inspection report about failure cause.

Interpretation\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1.4  Precedence between instruments\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere two or more instruments address the same asset, the order of precedence is: (a) a Technical Service Bulletin that names the serial range of the asset; (b) the Regional Addendum for the region in which the asset is installed; (c) this policy. A Bulletin that has been superseded has no effect, whether or not it remains published. Where the Bulletin document and the service system applicability index disagree, the Bulletin document governs; the index is maintained for reporting and is informational only.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Coverage\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1  Standard coverage period\\r\\n  \\r\\nUnless extended or varied by an instrument of higher precedence, an asset is covered for twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning, or six thousand (6,000) running hours, whichever occurs first.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3  Assets with no commissioning record\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere the commissioning record for an asset is absent from the asset registry, coverage cannot be determined. The claim is to be held and the commissioning certificate requested from the installing partner. The date of despatch or the date of installation must not be substituted for the date of commissioning.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Amounts payable\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.1  Labour\\r\\n  \\r\\nLabour is payable at the flat-rate allowance published for the operation code in the current Flat Rate Labour schedule, or at the hours actually claimed, whichever is the lesser. The rate applied is the regional labour rate in force on the date of repair.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.2  Parts\\r\\n  \\r\\nParts are payable at the published list price for the region, for the part actually fitted. Where a part has been superseded, the price of the superseding part applies.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.3  Handling\\r\\n  \\r\\nA handling uplift on parts is payable only where the partner\\u0027s Service Partner Agreement expressly grants one, at the percentage stated in that agreement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Exclusions\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.1  Exclusion - misuse and overload\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from operation outside the published duty envelope, including sustained overload, is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.2  Exclusion - fluid contamination\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from hydraulic fluid contamination above ISO 4406 class 18/16/13 is excluded, save where a Technical Service Bulletin provides otherwise.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.3  Exclusion - unauthorised modification\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from modification not authorised in writing by Contoso Industrial is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.4  Exclusion - consumables\\r\\n  \\r\\nFilters, fluids, belts, seals and other consumables are excluded when replaced as scheduled maintenance. Scheduled maintenance is not claimable under warranty and has no warranty operation code, so a consumable claimed under a warranty repair operation code is treated as a corrective repair and is covered, unless an inspection report records the replacement as routine.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 6. Repair warranty\\r\\n\\r\\n### 6.1  Repair warranty\\r\\n  \\r\\nA component replaced under warranty carries a further ninety (90) days of coverage from the date the repair was completed. A claim arising within that period is adjudicated under this clause and carries funding code RW, whether or not the underlying asset remains within its coverage period.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 7. Goodwill and authority\\r\\n\\r\\n### 7.1  Goodwill authority\\r\\n  \\r\\nAn amount payable outside coverage may be authorised as goodwill only by a person holding the tier of authority set out in the Goodwill and Authority Matrix for that amount, and only where the authority is recorded in the claim system. It applies to every claim submitted through the service claim system.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Interpretation\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1.4  Precedence between instruments\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere two or more instruments address the same asset, the order of precedence is: (a) a Technical Service Bulletin that names the serial range of the asset; (b) the Regional Addendum for the region in which the asset is installed; (c) this policy. A Bulletin that has been superseded has no effect, whether or not it remains published. Where the Bulletin document and the service system applicability index disagree, the Bulletin document governs; the index is maintained for reporting and is informational only.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Coverage\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1  Standard coverage period\\r\\n  \\r\\nUnless extended or varied by an instrument of higher precedence, an asset is covered for twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning, or six thousand (6,000) running hours, whichever occurs first.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3  Assets with no commissioning record\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere the commissioning record for an asset is absent from the asset registry, coverage cannot be determined. The claim is to be held and the commissioning certificate requested from the installing partner. The date of despatch or the date of installation must not be substituted for the date of commissioning.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Amounts payable\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.1  Labour\\r\\n  \\r\\nLabour is payable at the flat-rate allowance published for the operation code in the current Flat Rate Labour schedule, or at the hours actually claimed, whichever is the lesser. The rate applied is the regional labour rate in force on the date of repair.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.2  Parts\\r\\n  \\r\\nParts are payable at the published list price for the region, for the part actually fitted. Where a part has been superseded, the price of the superseding part applies.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.3  Handling\\r\\n  \\r\\nA handling uplift on parts is payable only where the partner\\u0027s Service Partner Agreement expressly grants one, at the percentage stated in that agreement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Exclusions\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.1  Exclusion - misuse and overload\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from operation outside the published duty envelope, including sustained overload, is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.2  Exclusion - fluid contamination\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from hydraulic fluid contamination above ISO 4406 class 18/16/13 is excluded, save where a Technical Service Bulletin provides otherwise.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.3  Exclusion - unauthorised modification\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from modification not authorised in writing by Contoso Industrial is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.4  Exclusion - consumables\\r\\n  \\r\\nFilters, fluids, belts, seals and other consumables are excluded when replaced as scheduled maintenance. Scheduled maintenance is not claimable under warranty and has no warranty operation code, so a consumable claimed under a warranty repair operation code is treated as a corrective repair and is covered, unless an inspection report records the replacement as routine.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 6. Repair warranty\\r\\n\\r\\n### 6.1  Repair warranty\\r\\n  \\r\\nA component replaced under warranty carries a further ninety (90) days of coverage from the date the repair was completed. A claim arising within that period is adjudicated under this clause and carries funding code RW, whether or not the underlying asset remains within its coverage period.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 7. Goodwill and authority\\r\\n\\r\\n### 7.1  Goodwill authority\\r\\n  \\r\\nAn amount payable outside coverage may be authorised as goodwill only by a person holding the tier of authority set out in the Goodwill and Authority Matrix for that amount, and only where the authority is recorded in the claim system. Response.Content:
## Decision: **Covered — approve INR 67,500**

Claim **C-2026-04118** is covered under **TSB-P-0112**, using **TSB funding**, subject to human review and release of the draft adjudication already recorded in the claim system.

The claim concerns a valve-plate replacement on serial **CIE-2200-AC-00600**, repaired **1 June 2026**, with **4.0 labour hours** and part **P-22450-C**.

### Why it is covered

- The asset is a **2200-AC air compressor** in Pune, India, commissioned **1 March 2024**.
- **TSB-P-0112**, effective 9 February 2026, covers the valve plate on 2200-series serials **CIE-2200-AC-00400 through CIE-2200-AC-00750**, inclusive. It extends coverage to **30 months from commissioning or 7,000 running hours, whichever occurs first**. Serial **00600** is within that range.
- On the repair date, the asset was **27 months from commissioning**, within the 30-month limit. Its latest reading at or before repair was **3,000 hours**, below the 7,000-hour limit.
- The normal India limit would be **18 months or 5,000 hours**, so the claim would be outside ordinary regional coverage. However, **POL-WAR-4.2 clause 1.4** gives the serial-specific TSB precedence over the regional addendum.
- Service history confirms operation **VALVE-PLT-RR**, actual part fitted **P-22450-C**, and actual labour of **4.0 hours**.

### Payable

| Element | Calculation | Payable |
|---|---:|---:|
| Labour | Lesser of 4.0 hours claimed and the 4.0-hour flat-rate allowance; 4.0 × INR 1,450/hour | **INR 5,800** |
| Part | P-22450-C, current India list price | **INR 61,700** |
| Partner handling uplift | Fabrikam SPA provides 0% | **INR 0** |
| **Total** | 5,800 + 61,700 | **INR 67,500** |

The labour schedule allows **4.0 hours** for VALVE-PLT-RR, and the India FY26 rate effective 1 April 2026 is **INR 1,450/hour**. The current price for P-22450-C is **INR 61,700**. Fabrikam’s partner agreement requires settlement in INR and provides no parts-handling uplift.

The claim was submitted on **7 June 2026**, six days after repair, so it met the partner’s 30-day submission requirement.

### Governing instruments

1. **TSB-P-0112** — controlling coverage instrument for this serial and valve-plate repair; funding code **TSB**.
2. **POL-WAR-4.2**, clauses **1.4, 4.1, 4.2, and 4.3** — establishes TSB precedence and the labour, parts, and handling calculation rules.
3. **ADD-IN-2.1** — establishes the ordinary India baseline, but is displaced by TSB-P-0112 for this repair.
4. **Flat-Rate-Labour-FY26**, **Labour-Rates-By-Region-FY26**, and **SPA-2023-FAB-IN** — determine the payable amount and partner-specific terms.

### Conflicts and next action

- The claim-system index also flags **TSB-P-0115**, but that bulletin is limited to **EMEA drive-train** coverage. The asset is in India, and the repair is for a valve plate, so it does not apply.
- **TSB-P-0107** must not be used because it was superseded by TSB-P-0112.
- No further evidence is required to determine coverage or calculate payment.
- Draft adjudication **ADJ-ECE1F311E5** has been recorded as **approve, INR 67,500**, under TSB-P-0112. It is awaiting human review; **no payment has yet been made**.

**Next action:** the assigned human adjudicator should review and release the draft approval under **TSB funding**. No goodwill approval or partner evidence request is needed.

It applies to every claim submitted through the service claim system.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Interpretation\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1.4  Precedence between instruments\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere two or more instruments address the same asset, the order of precedence is: (a) a Technical Service Bulletin that names the serial range of the asset; (b) the Regional Addendum for the region in which the asset is installed; (c) this policy. A Bulletin that has been superseded has no effect, whether or not it remains published. Where the Bulletin document and the service system applicability index disagree, the Bulletin document governs; the index is maintained for reporting and is informational only.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Coverage\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1  Standard coverage period\\r\\n  \\r\\nUnless extended or varied by an instrument of higher precedence, an asset is covered for twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning, or six thousand (6,000) running hours, whichever occurs first.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3  Assets with no commissioning record\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere the commissioning record for an asset is absent from the asset registry, coverage cannot be determined. The claim is to be held and the commissioning certificate requested from the installing partner. The date of despatch or the date of installation must not be substituted for the date of commissioning.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Amounts payable\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.1  Labour\\r\\n  \\r\\nLabour is payable at the flat-rate allowance published for the operation code in the current Flat Rate Labour schedule, or at the hours actually claimed, whichever is the lesser. The rate applied is the regional labour rate in force on the date of repair.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.2  Parts\\r\\n  \\r\\nParts are payable at the published list price for the region, for the part actually fitted. Where a part has been superseded, the price of the superseding part applies.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.3  Handling\\r\\n  \\r\\nA handling uplift on parts is payable only where the partner\\u0027s Service Partner Agreement expressly grants one, at the percentage stated in that agreement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Exclusions\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.1  Exclusion - misuse and overload\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from operation outside the published duty envelope, including sustained overload, is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.2  Exclusion - fluid contamination\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from hydraulic fluid contamination above ISO 4406 class 18/16/13 is excluded, save where a Technical Service Bulletin provides otherwise.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.3  Exclusion - unauthorised modification\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from modification not authorised in writing by Contoso Industrial is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.4  Exclusion - consumables\\r\\n  \\r\\nFilters, fluids, belts, seals and other consumables are excluded when replaced as scheduled maintenance. Scheduled maintenance is not claimable under warranty and has no warranty operation code, so a consumable claimed under a warranty repair operation code is treated as a corrective repair and is covered, unless an inspection report records the replacement as routine.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 6. Repair warranty\\r\\n\\r\\n### 6.1  Repair warranty\\r\\n  \\r\\nA component replaced under warranty carries a further ninety (90) days of coverage from the date the repair was completed. A claim arising within that period is adjudicated under this clause and carries funding code RW, whether or not the underlying asset remains within its coverage period.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 7. Goodwill and authority\\r\\n\\r\\n### 7.1  Goodwill authority\\r\\n  \\r\\nAn amount payable outside coverage may be authorised as goodwill only by a person holding the tier of authority set out in the Goodwill and Authority Matrix for that amount, and only where the authority is recorded in the claim system. Coverage\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1  Standard coverage period\\r\\n  \\r\\nUnless extended or varied by an instrument of higher precedence, an asset is covered for twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning, or six thousand (6,000) running hours, whichever occurs first.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3  Assets with no commissioning record\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere the commissioning record for an asset is absent from the asset registry, coverage cannot be determined. Where a part has been superseded, the price of the superseding part applies.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.3  Handling\\r\\n  \\r\\nA handling uplift on parts is payable only where the partner\\u0027s Service Partner Agreement expressly grants one, at the percentage stated in that agreement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Repair warranty\\r\\n\\r\\n### 6.1  Repair warranty\\r\\n  \\r\\nA component replaced under warranty carries a further ninety (90) days of coverage from the date the repair was completed. It applies to every claim submitted through the service claim system.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Interpretation\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1.4  Precedence between instruments\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere two or more instruments address the same asset, the order of precedence is: (a) a Technical Service Bulletin that names the serial range of the asset; (b) the Regional Addendum for the region in which the asset is installed; (c) this policy. A Bulletin that has been superseded has no effect, whether or not it remains published. Where the Bulletin document and the service system applicability index disagree, the Bulletin document governs; the index is maintained for reporting and is informational only.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Coverage\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1  Standard coverage period\\r\\n  \\r\\nUnless extended or varied by an instrument of higher precedence, an asset is covered for twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning, or six thousand (6,000) running hours, whichever occurs first.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3  Assets with no commissioning record\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere the commissioning record for an asset is absent from the asset registry, coverage cannot be determined. The claim is to be held and the commissioning certificate requested from the installing partner. The date of despatch or the date of installation must not be substituted for the date of commissioning.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Amounts payable\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.1  Labour\\r\\n  \\r\\nLabour is payable at the flat-rate allowance published for the operation code in the current Flat Rate Labour schedule, or at the hours actually claimed, whichever is the lesser. The rate applied is the regional labour rate in force on the date of repair.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.2  Parts\\r\\n  \\r\\nParts are payable at the published list price for the region, for the part actually fitted. Where a part has been superseded, the price of the superseding part applies.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.3  Handling\\r\\n  \\r\\nA handling uplift on parts is payable only where the partner\\u0027s Service Partner Agreement expressly grants one, at the percentage stated in that agreement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Exclusions\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.1  Exclusion - misuse and overload\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from operation outside the published duty envelope, including sustained overload, is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.2  Exclusion - fluid contamination\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from hydraulic fluid contamination above ISO 4406 class 18/16/13 is excluded, save where a Technical Service Bulletin provides otherwise.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.3  Exclusion - unauthorised modification\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from modification not authorised in writing by Contoso Industrial is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.4  Exclusion - consumables\\r\\n  \\r\\nFilters, fluids, belts, seals and other consumables are excluded when replaced as scheduled maintenance. Scheduled maintenance is not claimable under warranty and has no warranty operation code, so a consumable claimed under a warranty repair operation code is treated as a corrective repair and is covered, unless an inspection report records the replacement as routine.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 6. Repair warranty\\r\\n\\r\\n### 6.1  Repair warranty\\r\\n  \\r\\nA component replaced under warranty carries a further ninety (90) days of coverage from the date the repair was completed. A claim arising within that period is adjudicated under this clause and carries funding code RW, whether or not the underlying asset remains within its coverage period.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 7. Goodwill and authority\\r\\n\\r\\n### 7.1  Goodwill authority\\r\\n  \\r\\nAn amount payable outside coverage may be authorised as goodwill only by a person holding the tier of authority set out in the Goodwill and Authority Matrix for that amount, and only where the authority is recorded in the claim system. An approval given in conversation, in a channel message, or by telephone does not constitute authority for the purposes of this Execution.UserQuery: Is serial CIE-2200-AC-00800 still in warranty as at 2026-06-01? There's a claim, C-2026-04117.

Response.Content:
# Decision

**Serial CIE-2200-AC-00800 was not under warranty on 2026-06-01. Claim C-2026-04117 should be declined, subject to human review.** The asset had passed the governing India time limit even though it remained below the running-hours limit. No current bulletin or earlier warranty repair extends coverage to this valve-plate repair. I recorded **draft adjudication ADJ-C56F734175** as **decline, INR 0**; it is awaiting human review, and no payment or notification was made.

## 1. Asset and claim facts

- The asset is a **2200-AC air compressor** installed at **Litware Manufacturing, Pune, India**, by partner **D-IN-01**. It was installed on 2024-02-07 and **commissioned on 2024-03-01**. The commissioning date—not installation date—is the warranty start date.
- Claim **C-2026-04117** is currently **Submitted**. It concerns a **valve-plate replacement** under operation code `VALVE-PLT-RR`, repaired on **2026-06-01** and submitted on **2026-06-07**. It claims part **P-22450-C**, 4.0 labour hours, and no goodwill.
- Service history confirms that on 2026-06-01 the component actually repaired was the **valve plate**, part **P-22450-C** was fitted, and 4.0 labour hours were recorded.

## 2. Governing warranty instrument

The governing ordinary-coverage instrument is **ADD-IN-2.1 Regional Addendum – India**, read with **POL-WAR-4.2 Global Warranty Policy**:

1. Policy clause 1.4 sets the precedence order: an applicable serial-range TSB first, then the regional addendum, then the global policy. Superseded bulletins have no effect, and the bulletin document prevails over the service-system applicability index.
2. Because this asset is installed in India and no current component-specific TSB covers it, **ADD-IN-2.1 A1** varies the ordinary warranty to **18 months from commissioning or 5,000 running hours, whichever occurs first**.

## 3. Time and running-hours tests

| Test | Governing limit | Position at repair | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Time | 18 months from 2024-03-01 | Repair on 2026-06-01, exactly 27 months after commissioning | **Failed** — time coverage ended on 2025-09-01, nine months before the repair |
| Running hours | 5,000 hours | Latest reading at or before 2026-06-01: **3,000 hours** | **Passed** — 2,000 hours remained |

The India addendum applies the limits on a **whichever-occurs-first** basis. Passing the hours test therefore does not preserve coverage after the time limit has expired. The 3,000-hour reading exists in the claim system and is dated as of the repair date.

## 4. Bulletins

### TSB-P-0112 — does not apply

The current valve-plate bulletin, **TSB-P-0112**, covers 2200-series valve plates only for serials **CIE-2200-AC-00400 through CIE-2200-AC-00750**, with extended coverage of 30 months or 7,000 hours. Serial **00800 is outside that range**, so the bulletin does not extend this repair.

### TSB-P-0107 — cannot be used

The older valve-plate bulletin **TSB-P-0107** covered serials through 00900 and therefore would numerically have included 00800. However, the bulletin itself states that it was **superseded by TSB-P-0112, has no effect, and must not be used for adjudication**. Under policy clause 1.4, its former wider range cannot support this claim.

### TSB-P-0115 — index/document discrepancy; document governs

The service-system index reports serial 00800 as in range for **TSB-P-0115**. That is not sufficient: the authoritative bulletin document limits TSB-P-0115 to **EMEA only** and to the **drive motor/drive train**, whereas this asset is in India and the claim concerns the valve plate. It therefore does not apply. This is a source discrepancy, resolved in favour of the bulletin document under policy clause 1.4.

## 5. Repeat-repair coverage

Policy clause 6.1 gives a component replaced **under warranty** a further 90 days’ coverage from completion, under funding code RW.

No qualifying earlier valve-plate repair was found. The only job returned for this serial is the present 2026-06-01 repair associated with C-2026-04117; it is not an earlier repair capable of creating repeat-repair coverage for itself.

Because this repair is being declined as outside coverage, it also does not establish a new 90-day repair-warranty period under clause 6.1.

## 6. Claim status and financial implication

- **Current claim-system status:** Submitted.
- **Submission timing:** Six days after repair, which is within partner D-IN-01’s 30-day submission SLA; timely submission does not cure the expired warranty.
- **Warranty payable:** **INR 0** because the claim fails coverage.
- For transparency, the amount that would otherwise form the gross pricing basis is:
  - Labour: lesser of 4.0 hours claimed and the 4.0-hour flat-rate allowance = **4.0 × INR 1,450 = INR 5,800**.
  - Part: P-22450-C actually fitted, current India list price = **INR 61,700**.
  - Partner handling uplift: **0% = INR 0**.
  - Notional gross before the coverage decision: **INR 67,500**.
  - **Actual draft payable after decline: INR 0.**

## 7. Missing evidence, searches and next action

- **No evidence request is required to determine warranty:** the commissioning date and repair-date running-hours reading are both present.
- I did not locate an inspection report for this claim in the Warranty Operations evidence search. That does not prevent this time-based decision: the partner agreement says a missing inspection report does not itself hold a claim, unless an exclusion depends on it. Here, the claim already fails the coverage period without relying on an exclusion.
- Searches of Teams for the exact claim reference, serial number and TSB-P-0112 produced no matching messages; no channel-based exception or escalation was identified.
- **Next action:** the adjudicator should review and, if satisfied, approve draft **ADJ-C56F734175** as a decline. If the partner seeks goodwill, that would require a separate request and authority recorded in the claim system; none was requested on this claim. No final payment should be made and no party should be notified until human approval.

It applies to every claim submitted through the service claim system.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Interpretation\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1.4  Precedence between instruments\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere two or more instruments address the same asset, the order of precedence is: (a) a Technical Service Bulletin that names the serial range of the asset; (b) the Regional Addendum for the region in which the asset is installed; (c) this policy. A Bulletin that has been superseded has no effect, whether or not it remains published. Where the Bulletin document and the service system applicability index disagree, the Bulletin document governs; the index is maintained for reporting and is informational only.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Coverage\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1  Standard coverage period\\r\\n  \\r\\nUnless extended or varied by an instrument of higher precedence, an asset is covered for twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning, or six thousand (6,000) running hours, whichever occurs first.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3  Assets with no commissioning record\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere the commissioning record for an asset is absent from the asset registry, coverage cannot be determined. The claim is to be held and the commissioning certificate requested from the installing partner. The date of despatch or the date of installation must not be substituted for the date of commissioning.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Amounts payable\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.1  Labour\\r\\n  \\r\\nLabour is payable at the flat-rate allowance published for the operation code in the current Flat Rate Labour schedule, or at the hours actually claimed, whichever is the lesser. The rate applied is the regional labour rate in force on the date of repair.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.2  Parts\\r\\n  \\r\\nParts are payable at the published list price for the region, for the part actually fitted. Where a part has been superseded, the price of the superseding part applies.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.3  Handling\\r\\n  \\r\\nA handling uplift on parts is payable only where the partner\\u0027s Service Partner Agreement expressly grants one, at the percentage stated in that agreement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Exclusions\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.1  Exclusion - misuse and overload\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from operation outside the published duty envelope, including sustained overload, is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.2  Exclusion - fluid contamination\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from hydraulic fluid contamination above ISO 4406 class 18/16/13 is excluded, save where a Technical Service Bulletin provides otherwise.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.3  Exclusion - unauthorised modification\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from modification not authorised in writing by Contoso Industrial is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.4  Exclusion - consumables\\r\\n  \\r\\nFilters, fluids, belts, seals and other consumables are excluded when replaced as scheduled maintenance. Scheduled maintenance is not claimable under warranty and has no warranty operation code, so a consumable claimed under a warranty repair operation code is treated as a corrective repair and is covered, unless an inspection report records the replacement as routine.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 6. Repair warranty\\r\\n\\r\\n### 6.1  Repair warranty\\r\\n  \\r\\nA component replaced under warranty carries a further ninety (90) days of coverage from the date the repair was completed. A claim arising within that period is adjudicated under this clause and carries funding code RW, whether or not the underlying asset remains within its coverage period.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 7. Response.Content:
## Decision — decline; payable **INR 0**

Claim **C-2026-04116** should be **declined as outside the applicable warranty period**. The claim was submitted for a control-board replacement performed on **1 May 2026**, using operation **CTRL-BD-RR**, part **P-44900**, and **1.5 claimed labour hours**.

A **draft decline adjudication** has been recorded for human review as **ADJ-CF2BCD2F3D**, with payable **INR 0**. It is only a draft: no payment or partner notification has been made.

### Coverage and governing instruments

- The asset registry identifies serial **CIE-4000-CH-01950** as a **4000-CH** chiller installed in **Pune, India**, commissioned on **1 September 2024**.
- **ADD-IN-2.1, A1** governs the coverage period because this is an India installation. It varies the global baseline to **18 months from commissioning or 5,000 running hours, whichever occurs first**, with settlement in INR.
- The 18-month time limit reached its endpoint on **1 March 2026**. The repair on **1 May 2026** was therefore about two months outside time coverage.
- The latest claim-system reading at the repair date was **3,000 hours**, below the 5,000-hour limit, but the addendum uses the limit reached first; the earlier time expiry controls.
- **POL-WAR-4.2 clause 1.4** supplies the instrument-precedence rule and clauses **4.1–4.3** supply the valuation rules for labour, parts and partner handling.

### Bulletin review and preserved discrepancy

**TSB-C-0051 does not extend this claim.** The service-system bulletin index identified it as potentially relevant to the 4000-CH family and correctly marked this serial as out of range. The authoritative bulletin itself covers only serials **CIE-4000-CH-01200 through CIE-4000-CH-01850**, and only the **hydraulic circuit and compressor**. This asset is serial **-01950**, and the repaired component was **controls**.

Accordingly, there is **no conflict between the index and the bulletin for this claim**; both indicate that TSB-C-0051 is inapplicable. The bulletin document remains the authoritative source under policy clause 1.4.

### Payable calculation

Because the repair is outside coverage and no alternative coverage applies, the actual payable amount is:

| Element | Working | Payable |
|---|---:|---:|
| Labour | Outside coverage | INR 0 |
| Part | Outside coverage | INR 0 |
| Partner handling | Outside coverage | INR 0 |
| **Total** |  | **INR 0** |

For audit transparency, the claim’s **notional covered value** would have been **INR 69,575**:

- Labour: lesser of **1.5 hours claimed** and the **1.5-hour flat-rate allowance** = 1.5 hours; **1.5 × INR 1,450 = INR 2,175**. The FY26 schedule assigns 1.5 hours to CTRL-BD-RR, and the India rate in force on 1 May 2026 was INR 1,450/hour.
- Part: the service record confirms that **P-44900** was actually fitted, matching the claim. It is not superseded and carries an India list price of **INR 67,400**.
- Handling: **INR 0**. Fabrikam Service Partners’ agreement expressly provides no handling uplift; the claim-system partner record likewise shows **0%**.
- Notional total: **INR 2,175 + INR 67,400 + INR 0 = INR 69,575**.

Interpretation\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1.4  Precedence between instruments\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere two or more instruments address the same asset, the order of precedence is: (a) a Technical Service Bulletin that names the serial range of the asset; (b) the Regional Addendum for the region in which the asset is installed; (c) this policy. Coverage\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1  Standard coverage period\\r\\n  \\r\\nUnless extended or varied by an instrument of higher precedence, an asset is covered for twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning, or six thousand (6,000) running hours, whichever occurs first.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3  Assets with no commissioning record\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere the commissioning record for an asset is absent from the asset registry, coverage cannot be determined. # Claim C-2026-04115 — recommend APPROVE

**Recommendation:** Approve **INR 755,050** under **TSB-C-0051**, using **TSB funding**, subject to human review of the draft. The repair is covered because the asset’s serial is within the bulletin’s stated range, the failed/replaced component is the compressor, and the repair occurred before both the bulletin’s 36-month and 8,000-hour limits.

## 1. Facts relied on

- **Claim:** C-2026-04115, submitted **8 July 2026** for a repair completed **2 July 2026**; operation **COMP-RR**; **9.0 labour hours** claimed; part claimed **P-44310**.
- **Asset:** CIE-4000-CH-01640, family **4000-CH**, installed at Litware Manufacturing in **Pune, India**; commissioned **4 April 2024**.
- **Repair record:** The service history confirms a compressor replacement on **2 July 2026**, with **P-44310 actually fitted** and **9.0 labour hours** recorded. There is no mismatch between the part claimed and the part fitted.
- **Running hours:** The latest claim-system reading at or before repair was **4,237 hours on 4 June 2026**.
- **Partner:** Fabrikam Service Partners, D-IN-01; settlement currency **INR**; the master record shows **0% parts uplift** and a **30-day submission SLA**.

## 2. Coverage basis and governing instruments

### Controlling instrument: TSB-C-0051

TSB-C-0051 is current and applies to 4000-series chillers from serial **CIE-4000-CH-01200 through CIE-4000-CH-01850 inclusive**. It extends coverage for the **hydraulic circuit and compressor** to **36 months from commissioning or 8,000 running hours, whichever occurs first**, and directs claims to TSB funding. Serial **01640** falls within that range, and this claim concerns the compressor.

The bulletin takes precedence under **POL-WAR-4.2 clause 1.4**, which ranks a serial-specific TSB ahead of the regional addendum and global policy.

### Where the repair falls in the period

- Commissioning: **4 April 2024**.
- 36-month anniversary: **4 April 2027**.
- Repair: **2 July 2026** — approximately **26 months and 28 days after commissioning**, and about **276 days before** the 36-month anniversary.
- Latest eligible hours reading: **4,237**, leaving **3,763 hours** below the 8,000-hour ceiling.

Both limbs were therefore open at the repair date. No repair-warranty extension or goodwill route is needed.

For comparison, the ordinary India term under **ADD-IN-2.1** is only **18 months or 5,000 hours**. That time term would have expired in October 2025, but it is displaced for this compressor repair by the higher-precedence TSB.

## 3. Payable calculation

| Element | Working | Payable |
|---|---:|---:|
| Labour | Lesser of 9.0 hours claimed and 9.0-hour COMP-RR flat allowance = **9.0 h**; 9.0 × INR 1,450 FY26 India rate | **INR 13,050** |
| Part | P-44310 compressor module actually fitted; current India list price; no supersession | **INR 742,000** |
| Partner handling uplift | 0% × INR 742,000 under SPA-2023-FAB-IN | **INR 0** |
| **Total** | 13,050 + 742,000 + 0 | **INR 755,050** |

POL-WAR-4.2 clauses 4.1–4.3 require the lesser of claimed and flat-rate labour hours at the regional rate in force on the repair date, the regional list price for the part actually fitted, and a handling uplift only where the partner agreement grants one. The FY26 flat-rate schedule assigns **9.0 hours** to COMP-RR, and the India rate in force from 1 April 2026 is **INR 1,450/hour**. The claim system’s resolved part record prices P-44310 at **INR 742,000** and shows no supersession. The Fabrikam agreement expressly provides no handling uplift.

The claim was submitted **6 days after repair**, within the partner’s 30-day SLA.

## 4. Discrepancies and missing evidence

1. **Material TSB-index discrepancy:** the service claim system’s non-authoritative applicability index incorrectly ends the TSB-C-0051 range at serial 01500 and therefore says serial 01640 is out of range. The published bulletin extends through serial 01850 and expressly states that the bulletin document governs where the index disagrees; policy clause 1.4 says the same. The decision therefore follows the bulletin, not the index.
2. **No claim-specific inspection report found:** searches of the Warranty Operations library did not return an inspection report for C-2026-04115. This does **not** presently prevent adjudication: the service record confirms the compressor repair and fitted part, and the Fabrikam agreement says a missing inspection report does not itself hold a claim unless an exclusion depends on it. No contrary exclusion evidence was located.
3. **Hours-reading timing:** the 4,237-hour reading is dated 4 June, 28 days before repair, rather than the repair date itself. It is nevertheless the latest system reading at or before the repair date, which is the prescribed record to use under the partner agreement.
4. **Teams check:** no claim- or serial-specific Teams messages were found. There is therefore no channel evidence changing the recommendation; in any event, channel discussion would not override the formal instruments or constitute approval.

## 5. Action recorded and immediate next step

I recorded **DRAFT adjudication ADJ-270F61A95B** with:

- decision: **approve**;
- payable: **INR 755,050**;
- controlling reference: **TSB-C-0051**, with POL-WAR-4.2, ADD-IN-2.1, the FY26 rate cards and SPA-2023-FAB-IN also cited;
- note to use **TSB funding**;
- the index discrepancy, coverage dates/hours and full calculation documented.

**Immediate next step:** the adjudicator should review and release—or amend—the draft. **No payment has been made and no partner notification has been sent.**

Execution.UserQuery: C-2026-04114 came in from Fabrikam Service Partners this morning. Where do we land?

Response.Content:
## Recommended decision — approve INR 199,175

Approve claim **C-2026-04114** in full under **funding code TSB**, reference **TSB-C-0051**, subject to the adjudicator’s human review of the draft. The claim is for a hydraulic-pump replacement on asset **CIE-4000-CH-01700**, repaired on **18 June 2026** by Fabrikam Service Partners; the fitted part and recorded job both match the submitted operation **HYD-PUMP-RR**.

### Governing instruments

1. **TSB-C-0051 — Extended coverage: 4000-series hydraulic circuit and compressor** is the controlling coverage instrument. It is current, effective from 15 January 2026, applies to 4000-series chillers in serial range **CIE-4000-CH-01200 through CIE-4000-CH-01850 inclusive**, and extends hydraulic-circuit and compressor coverage to **36 months from commissioning or 8,000 running hours, whichever occurs first**. Serial **…01700** is within that range, and a hydraulic-pump replacement is a hydraulic-circuit repair. The bulletin requires approved claims to be recorded under funding code TSB with reference TSB-C-0051.
2. **POL-WAR-4.2 clause 1.4** gives a serial-specific TSB precedence over the regional addendum and global policy and says the bulletin document governs where it conflicts with the service-system applicability index. Clauses **4.1–4.3** govern labour, parts and handling.
3. **ADD-IN-2.1** applies because the asset is installed in Pune, India. Its ordinary period would be 18 months/5,000 hours, but that period is displaced for this hydraulic repair by TSB-C-0051. It also establishes INR as the regional currency.
4. **SPA-2023-FAB-IN** confirms Fabrikam as the authorised India partner, INR settlement, a 30-day submission period, and no parts-handling uplift.

### Coverage reasoning

- The asset was commissioned on **4 April 2024**. Thirty-six months therefore runs through **4 April 2027**. The repair on **18 June 2026** was approximately 26 months after commissioning and was within that calendar limit.
- The latest registered reading at or before the repair was **4,120 hours on 4 June 2026**, below the bulletin’s **8,000-hour** limit. The partner agreement directs adjudication using the latest claim-system reading at or before repair.
- The inspection report records a seized hydraulic pump, intact drive coupling, no external impact damage, and replacement with **P-44120-A**. It records no contamination, misuse, unauthorised modification or other exclusion-triggering fact.
- The claim was submitted on **24 June 2026**, six days after the repair, within Fabrikam’s 30-day submission requirement.
- **Source discrepancy:** the claim-system TSB index says serial 01700 is outside TSB-C-0051’s range because its reporting entry stops at 01500. The authoritative bulletin extends through 01850; under policy clause 1.4, the bulletin document controls.

### Payable calculation

| Element | Working | Payable |
|---|---:|---:|
| Labour | Lesser of 5.5 hours claimed and 5.5-hour FY26 flat-rate allowance = **5.5 hours** × India rate **INR 1,450/hour** in force on 18 June 2026 | **INR 7,975** |
| Part | One **P-44120-A**, the part actually fitted and current part number, at India list price | **INR 191,200** |
| Partner handling uplift | INR 191,200 × **0%** under SPA-2023-FAB-IN | **INR 0** |
| **Total** | INR 7,975 + INR 191,200 + INR 0 | **INR 199,175** |

The FY26 flat-rate schedule assigns **5.5 hours** to HYD-PUMP-RR; the India labour rate effective 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 is **INR 1,450/hour**. The parts master prices fitted/current part P-44120-A at **INR 191,200**, and Fabrikam’s agreement grants no uplift.

### Action recorded and next step

I recorded draft adjudication **ADJ-A73EE9CA6A** against the claim with decision **approve**, payable **INR 199,175**, the instruments above, and instructions to use **TSB funding code / TSB-C-0051**. Its status is **“Draft — awaiting human review”; no payment has been made**.

**Next action:** the assigned warranty adjudicator should review and approve that draft, confirm TSB-C-0051 funding coding, and release it through the normal payment workflow. No missing-evidence hold or goodwill escalation is warranted on the records reviewed.

Interpretation\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1.4  Precedence between instruments\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere two or more instruments address the same asset, the order of precedence is: (a) a Technical Service Bulletin that names the serial range of the asset; (b) the Regional Addendum for the region in which the asset is installed; (c) this policy. Where a part has been superseded, the price of the superseding part applies.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.3  Handling\\r\\n  \\r\\nA handling uplift on parts is payable only where the partner\\u0027s Service Partner Agreement expressly grants one, at the percentage stated in that agreement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Repair warranty\\r\\n\\r\\n### 6.1  Repair warranty\\r\\n  \\r\\nA component replaced under warranty carries a further ninety (90) days of coverage from the date the repair was completed. Interpretation\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1.4  Precedence between instruments\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere two or more instruments address the same asset, the order of precedence is: (a) a Technical Service Bulletin that names the serial range of the asset; (b) the Regional Addendum for the region in which the asset is installed; (c) this policy. Coverage\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1  Standard coverage period\\r\\n  \\r\\nUnless extended or varied by an instrument of higher precedence, an asset is covered for twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning, or six thousand (6,000) running hours, whichever occurs first.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3  Assets with no commissioning record\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere the commissioning record for an asset is absent from the asset registry, coverage cannot be determined. Where a part has been superseded, the price of the superseding part applies.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.3  Handling\\r\\n  \\r\\nA handling uplift on parts is payable only where the partner\\u0027s Service Partner Agreement expressly grants one, at the percentage stated in that agreement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Repair warranty\\r\\n\\r\\n### 6.1  Repair warranty\\r\\n  \\r\\nA component replaced under warranty carries a further ninety (90) days of coverage from the date the repair was completed. ## Decision — decline

Claim **C-2026-04110** should be **declined**, with **INR 0.00 payable**. Draft adjudication **ADJ-1637C2389F** was recorded for human review; it is only a draft, and **no payment or irreversible action was taken**.

## Governing instrument

The outcome turns on **ADD-IN-2.1, India Regional Addendum, A1**, read with the precedence rule in **POL-WAR-4.2 clause 1.4**. Because the asset is installed in Pune, India, A1 replaces the global baseline with coverage of **18 months from commissioning or 5,000 running hours, whichever occurs first**.

The unit was commissioned on **14 February 2023**, so time coverage ended on **14 August 2024**. The seal-kit repair occurred on **3 March 2026**, after expiration; the latest recorded reading at or before repair was also **5,935 hours**, exceeding the 5,000-hour limit by 935 hours.

It applies to every claim submitted through the service claim system.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Interpretation\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1.4  Precedence between instruments\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere two or more instruments address the same asset, the order of precedence is: (a) a Technical Service Bulletin that names the serial range of the asset; (b) the Regional Addendum for the region in which the asset is installed; (c) this policy. A Bulletin that has been superseded has no effect, whether or not it remains published. Where the Bulletin document and the service system applicability index disagree, the Bulletin document governs; the index is maintained for reporting and is informational only.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Coverage\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1  Standard coverage period\\r\\n  \\r\\nUnless extended or varied by an instrument of higher precedence, an asset is covered for twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning, or six thousand (6,000) running hours, whichever occurs first.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3  Assets with no commissioning record\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere the commissioning record for an asset is absent from the asset registry, coverage cannot be determined. The claim is to be held and the commissioning certificate requested from the installing partner. The date of despatch or the date of installation must not be substituted for the date of commissioning.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Amounts payable\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.1  Labour\\r\\n  \\r\\nLabour is payable at the flat-rate allowance published for the operation code in the current Flat Rate Labour schedule, or at the hours actually claimed, whichever is the lesser. The rate applied is the regional labour rate in force on the date of repair.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.2  Parts\\r\\n  \\r\\nParts are payable at the published list price for the region, for the part actually fitted. Where a part has been superseded, the price of the superseding part applies.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.3  Handling\\r\\n  \\r\\nA handling uplift on parts is payable only where the partner\\u0027s Service Partner Agreement expressly grants one, at the percentage stated in that agreement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Exclusions\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.1  Exclusion - misuse and overload\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from operation outside the published duty envelope, including sustained overload, is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.2  Exclusion - fluid contamination\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from hydraulic fluid contamination above ISO 4406 class 18/16/13 is excluded, save where a Technical Service Bulletin provides otherwise.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.3  Exclusion - unauthorised modification\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from modification not authorised in writing by Contoso Industrial is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.4  Exclusion - consumables\\r\\n  \\r\\nFilters, fluids, belts, seals and other consumables are excluded when replaced as scheduled maintenance. Scheduled maintenance is not claimable under warranty and has no warranty operation code, so a consumable claimed under a warranty repair operation code is treated as a corrective repair and is covered, unless an inspection report records the replacement as routine.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 6. Repair warranty\\r\\n\\r\\n### 6.1  Repair warranty\\r\\n  \\r\\nA component replaced under warranty carries a further ninety (90) days of coverage from the date the repair was completed. A claim arising within that period is adjudicated under this clause and carries funding code RW, whether or not the underlying asset remains within its coverage period.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 7.
