Interpretation\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1.4  Precedence between instruments\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere two or more instruments address the same asset, the order of precedence is: (a) a Technical Service Bulletin that names the serial range of the asset; (b) the Regional Addendum for the region in which the asset is installed; (c) this policy. A Bulletin that has been superseded has no effect, whether or not it remains published. Where the Bulletin document and the service system applicability index disagree, the Bulletin document governs; the index is maintained for reporting and is informational only.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Coverage\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1  Standard coverage period\\r\\n  \\r\\nUnless extended or varied by an instrument of higher precedence, an asset is covered for twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning, or six thousand (6,000) running hours, whichever occurs first.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3  Assets with no commissioning record\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere the commissioning record for an asset is absent from the asset registry, coverage cannot be determined. The claim is to be held and the commissioning certificate requested from the installing partner. The date of despatch or the date of installation must not be substituted for the date of commissioning.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Amounts payable\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.1  Labour\\r\\n  \\r\\nLabour is payable at the flat-rate allowance published for the operation code in the current Flat Rate Labour schedule, or at the hours actually claimed, whichever is the lesser. The rate applied is the regional labour rate in force on the date of repair.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.2  Parts\\r\\n  \\r\\nParts are payable at the published list price for the region, for the part actually fitted. Where a part has been superseded, the price of the superseding part applies.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.3  Handling\\r\\n  \\r\\nA handling uplift on parts is payable only where the partner\\u0027s Service Partner Agreement expressly grants one, at the percentage stated in that agreement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Exclusions\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.1  Exclusion - misuse and overload\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from operation outside the published duty envelope, including sustained overload, is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.2  Exclusion - fluid contamination\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from hydraulic fluid contamination above ISO 4406 class 18/16/13 is excluded, save where a Technical Service Bulletin provides otherwise.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.3  Exclusion - unauthorised modification\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from modification not authorised in writing by Contoso Industrial is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.4  Exclusion - consumables\\r\\n  \\r\\nFilters, fluids, belts, seals and other consumables are excluded when replaced as scheduled maintenance. Scheduled maintenance is not claimable under warranty and has no warranty operation code, so a consumable claimed under a warranty repair operation code is treated as a corrective repair and is covered, unless an inspection report records the replacement as routine.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 6. Repair warranty\\r\\n\\r\\n### 6.1  Repair warranty\\r\\n  \\r\\nA component replaced under warranty carries a further ninety (90) days of coverage from the date the repair was completed. A claim arising within that period is adjudicated under this clause and carries funding code RW, whether or not the underlying asset remains within its coverage period.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 7. Goodwill and authority\\r\\n\\r\\n### 7.1  Goodwill authority\\r\\n  \\r\\nAn amount payable outside coverage may be authorised as goodwill only by a person holding the tier of authority set out in the Goodwill and Authority Matrix for that amount, and only where the authority is recorded in the claim system. Execution.UserQuery: What's the position on C-2026-04109?

Response.Content:
## Decision — decline the warranty claim

**C-2026-04109 should be declined as outside warranty coverage.** The claim-system record is still **Submitted**, but I have recorded draft adjudication **ADJ-C726EB6C79** as **Decline — INR 0**, awaiting human review; no payment has been made.

### Basis of decision

- The claim is for a **control-board replacement (operation CTRL-BD-RR, part P-44900)** carried out on **10 May 2026** on chiller **CIE-4000-CH-01900** in Pune, India. The claim was submitted on **16 May 2026** by Fabrikam Service Partners.
- The asset was commissioned on **1 June 2023**.
- Because the asset is installed in India, **ADD-IN-2.1, clause A1** governs the coverage period: **18 months from commissioning or 5,000 running hours, whichever occurs first**. That time period ended on **1 December 2024**.
- The latest claim-system reading at or before the repair was **5,200 hours on 1 May 2026**, also above the 5,000-hour limit. The repair on 10 May 2026 was therefore outside **both** the time and running-hours limits.
- **TSB-C-0051 does not rescue the claim.** The authoritative bulletin applies only to serials **CIE-4000-CH-01200 through CIE-4000-CH-01850** and only extends coverage for the **hydraulic circuit and compressor**. This asset is serial **01900**, and the repair concerns the **control system**. Under POL-WAR-4.2 clause 1.4, the bulletin document—not the informational system index—governs applicability.
- No earlier covered replacement of P-44900 was found, so the separate **90-day repair warranty** under POL-WAR-4.2 clause 6.1 does not apply.
- The inspection report is present and confirms the control board was unresponsive, P-44900 was fitted, 1.5 labour hours were claimed, and there was no evidence of moisture ingress or surge damage. There is therefore no missing technical evidence affecting the decision.

### Payable amount

| Element | Payable |
|---|---:|
| Labour | INR 0 |
| Part P-44900 | INR 0 |
| Partner handling uplift | INR 0 |
| **Total** | **INR 0** |

Although the current India list price for P-44900 is INR 67,400, no part or labour reimbursement is payable because the repair is outside coverage. Fabrikam’s agreement provides **no handling uplift** in any event.

### Missing evidence / escalation

- **Missing evidence:** none identified.
- **Goodwill:** none was requested on the claim.
- **Escalation:** none is currently required or recorded. No Teams message referring to this claim was found, and there is no recorded goodwill authority to consider.

### Next step

The **human adjudicator** should review draft **ADJ-C726EB6C79** and, if satisfied, finalise the decline at **INR 0** and issue the decision to **Fabrikam Service Partners**. If the business wishes to consider an ex-contractual goodwill payment instead, that must be raised separately and approved at the appropriate tier in the claim system before any payment can be authorised; the present record provides no basis for goodwill.

Interpretation\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1.4  Precedence between instruments\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere two or more instruments address the same asset, the order of precedence is: (a) a Technical Service Bulletin that names the serial range of the asset; (b) the Regional Addendum for the region in which the asset is installed; (c) this policy. Coverage\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1  Standard coverage period\\r\\n  \\r\\nUnless extended or varied by an instrument of higher precedence, an asset is covered for twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning, or six thousand (6,000) running hours, whichever occurs first.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3  Assets with no commissioning record\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere the commissioning record for an asset is absent from the asset registry, coverage cannot be determined. Where a part has been superseded, the price of the superseding part applies.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.3  Handling\\r\\n  \\r\\nA handling uplift on parts is payable only where the partner\\u0027s Service Partner Agreement expressly grants one, at the percentage stated in that agreement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. # Claim C-2026-04103 — recommended decision: **APPROVE for INR 19,150**

Approve as a **standard warranty corrective repair**, not under a Technical Service Bulletin, repair warranty, or goodwill. The asset was within the India coverage limits on the repair date; the seal kit was claimed and recorded under a warranty repair operation code; and the available records contain no evidence that the replacement was scheduled maintenance or otherwise excluded.

## 1. Claim and asset facts

- Claim: **C-2026-04103**, submitted **28 April 2026** for a repair completed **22 April 2026**.
- Asset: **CIE-2200-AC-00320**, family **2200-AC**, installed at Litware Manufacturing, Pune, India.
- Commissioning date: **2 May 2025**; installation date: 9 April 2025. Coverage must run from commissioning, not installation.
- Repair: operation **SEAL-KIT-RR**, 3.0 labour hours claimed, part **P-22120**.
- Service history confirms that on 22 April 2026 the seals were repaired, **P-22120 was actually fitted**, 3.0 hours were worked, and the job was completed that day.
- Latest recorded usage at or before repair: **2,750 hours on 2 April 2026**.
- Service partner: **Fabrikam Service Partners (D-IN-01)**, settlement currency INR, with no parts-handling uplift.
- The claim was submitted six days after repair, within Fabrikam’s 30-day submission requirement.

## 2. Governing instruments and coverage

### Governing coverage instrument

**ADD-IN-2.1 Regional Addendum — India**, read with **POL-WAR-4.2 Global Warranty Policy**, governs. Policy clause 1.4 gives precedence to an applicable serial-range TSB, then the regional addendum, then the global policy. The India addendum varies the standard period to **18 months from commissioning or 5,000 running hours, whichever occurs first**.

Coverage therefore began on **2 May 2025** and, on the time limb, was scheduled to expire on **2 November 2026**, unless 5,000 hours was reached earlier. The repair on **22 April 2026** occurred about 11 months and 20 days after commissioning and **194 days before** the time-limit expiry. The latest permissible system reading was 2,750 hours, leaving **2,250 hours** beneath the 5,000-hour limit. Both limbs were therefore satisfied on the repair date.

### Why no TSB changes this result

The claim-system TSB index flags **TSB-P-0115** as in serial range, but the authoritative bulletin states that it applies **only to EMEA installations and only to the drive train**. This asset is in India and this claim concerns seals, so TSB-P-0115 does not apply. This is an index/bulletin applicability discrepancy; under policy clause 1.4, the bulletin document controls.

**TSB-P-0112** also does not apply: its authoritative range starts at CIE-2200-AC-00400, whereas this asset ends in **00320**, and it concerns the valve plate rather than seals. Its predecessor TSB-P-0107 is superseded and has no effect.

**TSB-P-0103** applies to all 2200-series serials but is advisory only: it addresses seal-kit part numbering and expressly does not vary warranty coverage. The fitted part is already the current part number, with no supersession in the parts record.

### Seal/consumable issue

Policy clause 5.4 excludes seals when replaced as scheduled maintenance. However, it also says that a consumable claimed under a warranty repair operation code is treated as a **corrective repair and covered**, unless an inspection report records the replacement as routine. Here, **SEAL-KIT-RR** is a published warranty operation code, and the service record confirms the corrective seal-kit replacement. No claim-specific inspection report was located, but Fabrikam’s agreement says a missing report does not itself hold a claim; it matters only where an exclusion depends on its contents. On the current record, there is no affirmative evidence of routine maintenance, misuse, overload, unauthorised modification, or another exclusion.

## 3. Payable amount

Under POL-WAR-4.2 clauses 4.1–4.3, labour is the lesser of claimed hours and the operation’s flat-rate allowance, paid at the regional rate in force on the repair date; parts are paid at the regional list price for the part actually fitted; handling is payable only if the partner agreement grants it.

| Element | Working | Payable |
|---|---:|---:|
| Labour | Lesser of 3.0 hours claimed and 3.0-hour FY26 allowance = 3.0 hours; 3.0 × INR 1,450 | **INR 4,350** |
| Part P-22120 | One seal kit actually fitted × current India list price INR 14,800 | **INR 14,800** |
| Partner handling uplift | INR 14,800 × 0%; SPA-2023-FAB-IN grants no uplift | **INR 0** |
| **Total** | 4,350 + 14,800 + 0 | **INR 19,150** |

Interpretation\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1.4  Precedence between instruments\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere two or more instruments address the same asset, the order of precedence is: (a) a Technical Service Bulletin that names the serial range of the asset; (b) the Regional Addendum for the region in which the asset is installed; (c) this policy. A Bulletin that has been superseded has no effect, whether or not it remains published. Coverage\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1  Standard coverage period\\r\\n  \\r\\nUnless extended or varied by an instrument of higher precedence, an asset is covered for twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning, or six thousand (6,000) running hours, whichever occurs first.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3  Assets with no commissioning record\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere the commissioning record for an asset is absent from the asset registry, coverage cannot be determined. The claim is to be held and the commissioning certificate requested from the installing partner. The date of despatch or the date of installation must not be substituted for the date of commissioning.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Amounts payable\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.1  Labour\\r\\n  \\r\\nLabour is payable at the flat-rate allowance published for the operation code in the current Flat Rate Labour schedule, or at the hours actually claimed, whichever is the lesser. It applies to every claim submitted through the service claim system.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Interpretation\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1.4  Precedence between instruments\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere two or more instruments address the same asset, the order of precedence is: (a) a Technical Service Bulletin that names the serial range of the asset; (b) the Regional Addendum for the region in which the asset is installed; (c) this policy. A Bulletin that has been superseded has no effect, whether or not it remains published. Where the Bulletin document and the service system applicability index disagree, the Bulletin document governs; the index is maintained for reporting and is informational only.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Coverage\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1  Standard coverage period\\r\\n  \\r\\nUnless extended or varied by an instrument of higher precedence, an asset is covered for twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning, or six thousand (6,000) running hours, whichever occurs first.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3  Assets with no commissioning record\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere the commissioning record for an asset is absent from the asset registry, coverage cannot be determined. The claim is to be held and the commissioning certificate requested from the installing partner. The date of despatch or the date of installation must not be substituted for the date of commissioning.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Amounts payable\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.1  Labour\\r\\n  \\r\\nLabour is payable at the flat-rate allowance published for the operation code in the current Flat Rate Labour schedule, or at the hours actually claimed, whichever is the lesser. The rate applied is the regional labour rate in force on the date of repair.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.2  Parts\\r\\n  \\r\\nParts are payable at the published list price for the region, for the part actually fitted. Where a part has been superseded, the price of the superseding part applies.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.3  Handling\\r\\n  \\r\\nA handling uplift on parts is payable only where the partner\\u0027s Service Partner Agreement expressly grants one, at the percentage stated in that agreement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Exclusions\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.1  Exclusion - misuse and overload\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from operation outside the published duty envelope, including sustained overload, is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.2  Exclusion - fluid contamination\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from hydraulic fluid contamination above ISO 4406 class 18/16/13 is excluded, save where a Technical Service Bulletin provides otherwise.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.3  Exclusion - unauthorised modification\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from modification not authorised in writing by Contoso Industrial is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.4  Exclusion - consumables\\r\\n  \\r\\nFilters, fluids, belts, seals and other consumables are excluded when replaced as scheduled maintenance. Scheduled maintenance is not claimable under warranty and has no warranty operation code, so a consumable claimed under a warranty repair operation code is treated as a corrective repair and is covered, unless an inspection report records the replacement as routine.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 6. Repair warranty\\r\\n\\r\\n### 6.1  Repair warranty\\r\\n  \\r\\nA component replaced under warranty carries a further ninety (90) days of coverage from the date the repair was completed. A claim arising within that period is adjudicated under this clause and carries funding code RW, whether or not the underlying asset remains within its coverage period.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 7. Goodwill and authority\\r\\n\\r\\n### 7.1  Goodwill authority\\r\\n  \\r\\nAn amount payable outside coverage may be authorised as goodwill only by a person holding the tier of authority set out in the Goodwill and Authority Matrix for that amount, and only where the authority is recorded in the claim system. Interpretation\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1.4  Precedence between instruments\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere two or more instruments address the same asset, the order of precedence is: (a) a Technical Service Bulletin that names the serial range of the asset; (b) the Regional Addendum for the region in which the asset is installed; (c) this policy. Coverage\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1  Standard coverage period\\r\\n  \\r\\nUnless extended or varied by an instrument of higher precedence, an asset is covered for twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning, or six thousand (6,000) running hours, whichever occurs first.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3  Assets with no commissioning record\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere the commissioning record for an asset is absent from the asset registry, coverage cannot be determined. The rate applied is the regional labour rate in force on the date of repair.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.2  Parts\\r\\n  \\r\\nParts are payable at the published list price for the region, for the part actually fitted. Where a part has been superseded, the price of the superseding part applies.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.3  Handling\\r\\n  \\r\\nA handling uplift on parts is payable only where the partner\\u0027s Service Partner Agreement expressly grants one, at the percentage stated in that agreement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Exclusions\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.1  Exclusion - misuse and overload\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from operation outside the published duty envelope, including sustained overload, is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.2  Exclusion - fluid contamination\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from hydraulic fluid contamination above ISO 4406 class 18/16/13 is excluded, save where a Technical Service Bulletin provides otherwise.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.3  Exclusion - unauthorised modification\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from modification not authorised in writing by Contoso Industrial is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.4  Exclusion - consumables\\r\\n  \\r\\nFilters, fluids, belts, seals and other consumables are excluded when replaced as scheduled maintenance. Scheduled maintenance is not claimable under warranty and has no warranty operation code, so a consumable claimed under a warranty repair operation code is treated as a corrective repair and is covered, unless an inspection report records the replacement as routine.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 6. Repair warranty\\r\\n\\r\\n### 6.1  Repair warranty\\r\\n  \\r\\nA component replaced under warranty carries a further ninety (90) days of coverage from the date the repair was completed. A claim arising within that period is adjudicated under this clause and carries funding code RW, whether or not the underlying asset remains within its coverage period.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 7. Execution.UserQuery: Fabrikam Service Partners have submitted C-2026-04102. Is it covered, and what do we pay?

Response.Content:
# Claim C-2026-04102 — assessment

## Decision

**Approve as a standard warranty claim for INR 48,420.**

The condenser-fan repair was carried out while the asset was within the India coverage limit of **18 months from commissioning or 5,000 running hours, whichever occurs first**. The repair occurred on **18 February 2026**, 13 months and 10 days after commissioning, and the latest qualifying meter record was **1,900 hours**. No applicable bulletin extends or displaces that standard India coverage for this component and serial.

## Governing instruments and why they apply

1. **ADD-IN-2.1 Regional Addendum — India, A1** governs the coverage period because the asset is installed at Pune, India. It varies the global baseline to **18 months / 5,000 hours, whichever occurs first**.
2. **POL-WAR-4.2 Global Warranty Policy**, particularly clauses **1.4, 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3**, governs instrument precedence and the calculation of labour, parts and handling. Under clause 1.4, a regional addendum takes precedence over the global baseline unless an applicable serial-specific bulletin governs.
3. **SPA-2023-FAB-IN**, Fabrikam Service Partners’ agreement, confirms INR settlement, a 30-day submission requirement, use of the latest running-hours reading at or before repair, reimbursement at the flat-rate labour allowance, and **no parts handling uplift**.
4. **TSB-C-0047** concerns condenser-fan balancing for all 4000-series chillers but is expressly advisory and does **not** vary warranty coverage.
5. **TSB-C-0051 does not apply**: its authoritative document covers serials **CIE-4000-CH-01200 through CIE-4000-CH-01850** and only the hydraulic circuit and compressor. This asset is serial **CIE-4000-CH-01052**, and the repair is a condenser-fan/structure repair.

## Coverage working

- Asset: **4000-CH industrial chiller, serial CIE-4000-CH-01052**, installed at Litware Manufacturing, Pune.
- Commissioned: **8 January 2025**.
- India time limit: **18 months**, therefore through **8 July 2026**, subject to the earlier running-hours limit.
- Repair: **18 February 2026**, within the time limit by approximately 4 months and 20 days. The claim-system record identifies operation **COND-FAN-RR**, part **P-44520**, and **3.5 labour hours**.
- Latest meter reading at or before repair: **1,900 hours on 8 February 2026**, below the 5,000-hour limit by 3,100 hours. The partner agreement requires this latest pre-repair reading to be used.
- Submission: **24 February 2026**, six days after repair and therefore within Fabrikam’s 30-day submission term.
- Service history confirms that the part actually fitted was **P-44520**, matching the claimed part, and records 3.5 hours for the same repair.

## Payable calculation

| Element | Working | Payable |
|---|---:|---:|
| Labour | lesser of 3.5 hours claimed and 3.5 flat-rate hours × INR 1,320/hour | **INR 4,620** |
| Parts | 1 × P-44520 condenser fan assembly at India list price INR 43,800 | **INR 43,800** |
| Partner handling uplift | INR 43,800 × 0% under SPA-2023-FAB-IN | **INR 0** |
| **Total** | INR 4,620 + INR 43,800 + INR 0 | **INR 48,420** |

The flat-rate schedule lists **3.5 hours** for COND-FAN-RR. Policy clause 4.1 caps labour at the lesser of the flat-rate allowance and hours claimed; both are 3.5. The India rate in force on the repair date was **INR 1,320/hour** for 1 April 2025–31 March 2026.

The parts list and claim-system parts record both identify P-44520 at **INR 43,800**, with no supersession. Policy clause 4.2 prices the part actually fitted.

Fabrikam’s agreement expressly says no handling uplift is payable; the dealer master also records a 0% uplift.

## Evidence gaps and source checks

- I did **not** locate an inspection report specifically for C-2026-04102 in the Warranty Operations library. This does not prevent determination here: the partner agreement says a missing inspection report does not itself hold a claim, and the claim-system and completed-job records agree on the repair, fitted part and labour hours. No fact currently indicates that an exclusion depends on an inspection finding.
- No Teams message was found for the claim reference, serial or condenser-fan issue. There is therefore no separate channel escalation or purported approval to reconcile.
- The service-system bulletin index is informational only. Its TSB-C-0051 entry says this serial is not in range, which agrees with the authoritative bulletin document; the document independently confirms the lower bound is CIE-4000-CH-01200.
- The FY26 flat-rate schedule located in the library is marked effective 1 April 2026, after the repair date. It states the same 3.5-hour allowance as the 3.5 hours claimed and recorded, so the payable labour quantity is 3.5 hours either way; the monetary rate is separately and expressly fixed by the repair-date regional schedule at INR 1,320/hour.

## Next steps

1. **Adjudicator:** approve C-2026-04102 as **standard warranty**, payable **INR 48,420**.
2. **Claim processor:** enter the breakdown as labour INR 4,620, parts INR 43,800 and handling INR 0; use the standard warranty funding route, not TSB, repair-warranty or goodwill.
3. **No partner action is required** before decision: commissioning and pre-repair hours are present, the claim was timely, and the fitted part is established in service history.
4. **No adjudication was created or recorded.** This response is an assessment only.

## Sources

1. `claim` Referenced tool result
2. `asset` Referenced tool result
3. `hours` Referenced tool result
4. `india-addendum` [ADD-IN-2.1 Regional Addendum — India v2.1](<https://microsoftapc.sharepoint.com/teams/ContosoFieldService/Warranty Operations/01-Policy/ADD-IN-2.1 Regional Addendum - India v2.1.docx>)
5. `global-policy` [POL-WAR-4.2 Contoso Industrial Global Warranty Policy v4.2](<https://microsoftapc.sharepoint.com/teams/ContosoFieldService/Warranty Operations/01-Policy/POL-WAR-4.2 Contoso Industrial Global Warranty Policy v4.2.docx>)
6. `fabrikam-spa` [SPA-2023-FAB-IN Fabrikam Service Partners](<https://microsoftapc.sharepoint.com/teams/ContosoFieldService/Warranty Operations/04-PartnerAgreements/SPA-2023-FAB-IN Fabrikam Service Partners.docx>)
7. `fan-bulletin` [TSB-C-0047 Condenser fan balancing procedure](<https://microsoftapc.sharepoint.com/teams/ContosoFieldService/Warranty Operations/02-Bulletins/TSB-C-0047 Condenser fan balancing procedure.docx>)
8. `extended-tsb` [TSB-C-0051 Extended coverage — 4000-series hydraulic circuit and compressor](<https://microsoftapc.sharepoint.com/teams/ContosoFieldService/Warranty Operations/02-Bulletins/TSB-C-0051 Extended coverage - 4000-series hydraulic circuit and compre.docx>)
9. `service-history` Referenced tool result

Industrial provides on equipment it manufactures, the basis on which a claim from an authorised service partner is adjudicated, and the amounts payable. It applies to every claim submitted through the service claim system.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Interpretation\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1.4  Precedence between instruments\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere two or more instruments address the same asset, the order of precedence is: (a) a Technical Service Bulletin that names the serial range of the asset; (b) the Regional Addendum for the region in which the asset is installed; (c) this policy. A Bulletin that has been superseded has no effect, whether or not it remains published. Where the Bulletin document and the service system applicability index disagree, the Bulletin document governs; the index is maintained for reporting and is informational only.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Coverage\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1  Standard coverage period\\r\\n  \\r\\nUnless extended or varied by an instrument of higher precedence, an asset is covered for twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning, or six thousand (6,000) running hours, whichever occurs first.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3  Assets with no commissioning record\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere the commissioning record for an asset is absent from the asset registry, coverage cannot be determined. The claim is to be held and the commissioning certificate requested from the installing partner. The date of despatch or the date of installation must not be substituted for the date of commissioning.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Amounts payable\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.1  Labour\\r\\n  \\r\\nLabour is payable at the flat-rate allowance published for the operation code in the current Flat Rate Labour schedule, or at the hours actually claimed, whichever is the lesser. The rate applied is the regional labour rate in force on the date of repair.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.2  Parts\\r\\n  \\r\\nParts are payable at the published list price for the region, for the part actually fitted. Where a part has been superseded, the price of the superseding part applies.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.3  Handling\\r\\n  \\r\\nA handling uplift on parts is payable only where the partner\\u0027s Service Partner Agreement expressly grants one, at the percentage stated in that agreement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Exclusions\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.1  Exclusion - misuse and overload\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from operation outside the published duty envelope, including sustained overload, is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.2  Exclusion - fluid contamination\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from hydraulic fluid contamination above ISO 4406 class 18/16/13 is excluded, save where a Technical Service Bulletin provides otherwise.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.3  Exclusion - unauthorised modification\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from modification not authorised in writing by Contoso Industrial is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.4  Exclusion - consumables\\r\\n  \\r\\nFilters, fluids, belts, seals and other consumables are excluded when replaced as scheduled maintenance. Scheduled maintenance is not claimable under warranty and has no warranty operation code, so a consumable claimed under a warranty repair operation code is treated as a corrective repair and is covered, unless an inspection report records the replacement as routine.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 6. Repair warranty\\r\\n\\r\\n### 6.1  Repair warranty\\r\\n  \\r\\nA component replaced under warranty carries a further ninety (90) days of coverage from the date the repair was completed. A claim arising within that period is adjudicated under this clause and carries funding code RW, whether or not the underlying asset remains within its coverage period.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 7. Goodwill and authority\\r\\n\\r\\n### 7.1  Goodwill authority\\r\\n  \\r\\nAn amount payable outside coverage may be authorised as goodwill only by a person holding the tier of authority set out in the Goodwill and Authority Matrix for that amount, and only where the authority is recorded in the claim system. # Claim C-2026-04101 — draft adjudication

## Decision: **Approve — covered**

Approve **INR 69,575** in total, subject to human adjudicator review. I recorded draft adjudication **ADJ-5165D9C52C** with decision `approve`; its status is **“Draft — awaiting human review. No payment has been made.”**

The submitted claim is for a control-board replacement on asset **CIE-4000-CH-01050**, repaired on **10 May 2026** by **Fabrikam Service Partners (D-IN-01)**. The claim was submitted on **16 May 2026**, six days after repair.

## Governing warranty instruments

1. **ADD-IN-2.1 Regional Addendum — India, clause A1** governs the coverage period because the asset is installed in **Pune, India**. It varies the global standard to **18 months from commissioning or 5,000 running hours, whichever occurs first**.
2. **POL-WAR-4.2 Global Warranty Policy**, read with the India addendum, governs precedence and valuation:
   - clause 1.4: bulletin → regional addendum → global policy;
   - clause 4.1: labour is the lesser of claimed or flat-rate hours, using the regional rate in force on the repair date;
   - clause 4.2: reimburse the regional list price of the part actually fitted, using the superseding part’s price if applicable;
   - clause 4.3: a parts-handling uplift is payable only if expressly granted by the partner agreement.
3. **SPA-2023-FAB-IN** confirms INR settlement, a 30-day submission requirement, use of the latest claim-system running-hours reading at or before repair, and **no handling uplift** for Fabrikam.
4. **TSB-C-0051 does not govern this repair.** The authoritative bulletin applies only to serials **CIE-4000-CH-01200 through CIE-4000-CH-01850**, while this asset is serial **01050**. It also extends coverage only for the **hydraulic circuit and compressor**, whereas this claim concerns the **controls/control board**.
5. **TSB-C-0038**, although applicable to all 4000-series serials as a control-board firmware advisory, expressly makes **no change to warranty coverage or claim handling**.

## Coverage calculation

- Commissioning date: **15 March 2025**.
- India time limit: 18 months, therefore coverage runs through **15 September 2026**.
- Repair date: **10 May 2026**, approximately four months before the time expiry.
- Latest claim-system reading at or before repair: **2,229 hours on 15 April 2026**, below the **5,000-hour** limit.
- Consequently, neither the time limit nor the running-hours limit had been reached when the repair occurred.
- The service history confirms that on 10 May 2026 the partner completed operation **CTRL-BD-RR**, fitted **P-44900**, and recorded **1.5 labour hours**.
- The claim was submitted six days after repair, within Fabrikam’s 30-day SLA.
- No earlier warranty replacement of P-44900 was found, so the separate 90-day repair-warranty provision is not the basis for approval.

## Payable amount

| Element | Working | Payable |
|---|---:|---:|
| Labour | Lesser of 1.5 hours claimed and 1.5-hour FY26 flat rate = **1.5 h** × **INR 1,450/h** | **INR 2,175** |
| Part | One control board **P-44900**, the part actually fitted; current India list price; no supersession | **INR 67,400** |
| Partner handling uplift | INR 67,400 × **0%** under SPA-2023-FAB-IN | **INR 0** |
| **Total** | INR 2,175 + INR 67,400 + INR 0 | **INR 69,575** |

The FY26 flat-rate schedule assigns **1.5 hours** to CTRL-BD-RR, and the India labour rate in force from 1 April 2026 is **INR 1,450 per hour**. The parts record identifies P-44900 as the control board for family 4000-CH, shows no supersession, and gives its current India price as **INR 67,400**. Fabrikam’s master record and agreement both state **0% handling uplift** and INR settlement.

## Rationale and claim evidence

The inspection report matches the claim and service record on the serial number, repair date, operation, fitted part and labour. It records an unresponsive control board, replacement of P-44900, and **no evidence of moisture ingress or surge damage**. No applicable warranty exclusion was established.

## Evidence gaps and discrepancies

- **Running-hours discrepancy:** the inspection report says **2,400 hours**, while the latest claim-system reading at or before the repair is **2,229 hours**. Under SPA-2023-FAB-IN, adjudication uses the claim-system reading. The discrepancy does **not** affect the outcome because both figures are well below 5,000 hours, but it should remain noted in the audit trail.
- **TSB applicability-index discrepancy:** the claim-system index lists TSB-C-0051 with a serial range ending at **01500**, while the authoritative bulletin ends at **01850**. Under policy clause 1.4, the bulletin document governs. The discrepancy is immaterial here because serial 01050 is below both lower bounds and the claimed controls repair is outside that bulletin’s component scope.
- **No blocking evidence gap:** commissioning date, qualifying system hours, repair date, fitted part, labour, applicable rate, partner terms and inspection findings are all available. No evidence request or goodwill escalation is appropriate.

## Next steps

1. **Human adjudicator:** review draft **ADJ-5165D9C52C** and, if satisfied, approve it through the normal claim workflow.
2. **Warranty Operations / system-data owner:** reconcile the inspection report’s 2,400-hour figure with the claim-system reading of 2,229 hours and correct the TSB-C-0051 applicability-index upper bound. These are audit/data-quality actions and need not hold this claim.
3. **Do not treat this as payment or notification:** only a draft adjudication was recorded; **no payment was made and the claimant was not notified**.
